content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To fix nail clippers, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Inspect the clipper for rust or misalignment (5 minutes)
Step 2. Soak the lever in a degreasing solution (15 minutes)
Step 3. Apply a drop of machine oil to the pin (2 minutes)
Step 4. Test the spring tension (1 minute)
Step 5. Sand down the rough edges of the cutting blades (10 minutes)
Step 6. Realign the top and bottom cutting edges (10 minutes)
Step 7. Buff the outer casing for a smooth finish (5 minutes)
Step 8. Tighten the central rivet (3 minutes)
Step 9. Polish the interior of the jaw (8 minutes)
Step 10. Locate a replacement pivot pin (20 minutes)
Step 11. Check the lever's rotational clearance (2 minutes)
Step 12. Retrieve a small wire brush (5 minutes)
Step 13. Clean the pivot hole with a cotton swab (3 minutes)
Step 14. Clear away metal shavings (4 minutes)
Step 15. Wipe down the lever with a microfiber cloth (2 minutes)
Step 16. Measure the gap between the blades (5 minutes)
Step 17. Verify the jaw closure is airtight (2 minutes)
Step 18. Lubricate the hinge joint (1 minute)
Step 19. Submerge the clipper body in a cleaning bath (30 minutes)
Step 20. Dry the components with compressed air (2 minutes)
Step 21. Perform a final cut test on a sample material (1 minute)
Step 22. Adjust the curvature of the blade (12 minutes)
Step 23. Remove the old, broken pin (10 minutes)
Step 24. Straighten the metal handle (7 minutes)
Step 25. Sharpen the file attachment (15 minutes)
Step 26. Degunk the inner spring mechanism (8 minutes)
Step 27. Gather the necessary repair tools (10 minutes)
Step 28. Store the sharpening stone (1 minute)
Step 29. Examine the clipper under a magnifying glass (5 minutes)
Step 30. Purchase a specialized repair kit (1 day)
Step 31. Unpack the repair kit components (5 minutes)
Step 32. Label the spare parts (10 minutes)
Step 33. Clean the work surface (5 minutes)
Step 34. Sanitize the blades with alcohol (5 minutes)
Step 35. Disassemble the main assembly (15 minutes)
Step 36. Check for hairline fractures in the steel (10 minutes)
Step 37. Smooth the pivot point with a needle file (12 minutes)
Step 38. Scrub the lever with a wire brush (6 minutes)
Step 39. Deburr the edges of the pin hole (4 minutes)
Step 40. Apply a protective anti-rust coating (1 hour)
Step 41. Allow the coating to cure (4 hours)
Step 42. Calibrate the lever's fulcrum point (15 minutes)
Step 43. Inspect the final alignment under bright light (5 minutes)
Step 44. Tension the cross-bar (6 minutes)
Step 45. Wash off any remaining abrasive paste (3 minutes)
Step 46. Flatten the base of the clipper (20 minutes)
Step 47. Fine-tune the blade sharpness with a ceramic rod (20 minutes)
Step 48. Re-insert the spring into the slot (5 minutes)
Step 49. Tap the pivot pin into place (2 minutes)
Step 50. Set up a bright workspace (15 minutes)
Step 51. Wash the components in warm soapy water (10 minutes)
Step 52. Remove any deep pitting from the metal (25 minutes)
Step 53. Heat the metal slightly to ease adjustments (10 minutes)
Step 54. Remove stubborn oxidation with vinegar (30 minutes)
Step 55. Rinse the lever thoroughly (2 minutes)
Step 56. Straighten the catching tray (5 minutes)
Step 57. Organize the work area (10 minutes)
Step 58. Clean the handle's grip surface (5 minutes)
Step 59. Dry the pivot area completely (5 minutes)
Step 60. Check the assembly for any rattling (2 minutes)
Step 61. Identify the specific model for specs (10 minutes)
Step 62. Find the instruction manual (15 minutes)
Step 63. Remove the built-in nail file (3 minutes)
Step 64. Prepare the compressed air canister (1 minute)
Step 65. Sterilize the entire unit (15 minutes)
Step 66. Mix a cleaning solution (5 minutes)
Step 67. Perform a safety check on the lever (2 minutes)
Step 68. Clear the workbench of debris (5 minutes)
Step 69. Apply a thin layer of wax to the body (10 minutes)
Step 70. Watch a tutorial on clipper repair (15 minutes)
Step 71. Hone the blades with a leather strop (10 minutes)
Step 72. Gather cleaning supplies (5 minutes)
Step 73. Reattach the handle to the base (5 minutes)
Step 74. Buff the cutting edge to a mirror finish (15 minutes)
Step 75. Select the appropriate pliers (2 minutes)
Step 76. Reassemble the lever and pin (10 minutes)
Step 77. Check the spring's responsiveness (2 minutes)
Step 78. Remove any excess oil (3 minutes)
Step 79. Inspect the tension bar for bends (8 minutes)
Step 80. Measure the lever's angle of lift (5 minutes)
